issues.legal_issue: A claim seeking possession of a building together with its appurtenant land may be adjudicated by the specialized tribunal when the governing definition of land includes buildings and structures attached to the earth.
material_facts: The application alleged that the respondent had forcibly occupied a house and its appurtenant open land.
The disputed property included both a building attached to the earth and a substantial area of open land.
The application sought possession of the house and the open land under the land-grabbing legislation.
The High Court treated a claim for a building with appurtenant land as outside the tribunal’s jurisdiction, distinguishing it from a claim for land with a building on it.
issues.conclusion: The application was maintainable before the Special Tribunal, which had jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute; the distinction between a building with appurtenant land and land with a building was artificial.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(c) and 2(e) of the Andhra Pradesh Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982, land includes buildings and structures attached to the earth, and land grabbing includes the unauthorized taking of possession of land. Accordingly, grabbing a building attached to the earth, including where the claim concerns the building and its appurtenant land, may constitute land grabbing for the purposes of the Act. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: special_land_grabbing_proceeding and (disputed_property_includes_attached_building and disputed_property_includes_land) and alleged_unauthorized_occupation

predicates.special_land_grabbing_proceeding: The claim was brought in a proceeding before a tribunal empowered to adjudicate allegations of land grabbing.
predicates.disputed_property_includes_attached_buil: The disputed property included a building attached to the earth.
predicates.disputed_property_includes_land: The disputed property included land on which the building stood or land appurtenant to it.
predicates.alleged_unauthorized_occupation: The applicant alleged that another person occupied the disputed property without lawful entitlement.

issues.definition: When a land-grabbing proceeding concerns alleged unauthorized occupation of both an attached building and land, the application is within the tribunal’s jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A later bench of a High Court of equal strength that disagrees with the legal view of an earlier co-ordinate bench must refer the issue to a larger bench rather than overrule that view.
material_facts: An earlier High Court bench had considered the tribunal’s jurisdiction and interpreted the governing definition of land in relation to the disputed property.
A later High Court bench reconsidered the same jurisdictional issue and reached a contrary view.
The later bench did not refer the issue to a larger bench before departing from the earlier bench’s legal view.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming the earlier decision did not operate as res judicata, judicial discipline required the later bench to refer the issue to a larger bench; it was not entitled to overrule the statement of law by a co-ordinate bench.
issues.legal_principle: A Division Bench’s statement of law binds a Division Bench of the same or lesser strength. If a later co-ordinate bench doubts or disagrees with that law, the accepted practice is to refer the matter to a larger bench rather than decide the correctness of the earlier view. This principle, supported by Union of India v. Raghubir Singh (1989) 2 SCC 754 and Central Board of Dawoodi Bohra Community v. State of Maharashtra (2005) 2 SCC 673, applies equally to High Courts.

predicates.later_high_court_panel: A later panel of a High Court considered a legal issue in a judicial proceeding.
predicates.earlier_equal_strength_panel_decided_sam: An earlier panel of the same court with equal strength had decided the same legal issue.
predicates.later_panel_disagrees: The later panel reached a view that conflicts with the earlier panel’s legal view.

issues.definition: If a later High Court panel disagrees with an earlier equal-strength panel on the same legal issue, the issue is to be referred to a larger bench.
